correctness.rationale: For a,b>=1, the one-hub subcomplex admits explicit free-face pair collapses onto the full leaf simplex. The relative simplicial chains are a shifted augmented leaf skeleton with sign from the two-hub orientation. Integral contraction by coordinate sum has kernel wedge^{r-2} of the augmentation lattice in the unique relevant degree; lower chains are exact, and the end cases are contractible. Maschke/transfer and the block-decomposition of the augmentation module prove the full-automorphism rational quotient. The attached independent verifier passes 112 face enumerations, 6210 actual elementary collapses, 84 full F2 homology computations, 266 character checks and 36 quotient checks. General proof, not finite tests, establishes the unbounded ranges.

originality.rationale: A decisive exact earlier theorem, Deshpande and Singh Theorem 3.10, already gives the full nonequivariant double-star sphere-wedge count; that statement is not claimed new. The narrowed scientific claim is the explicit integral signed exterior-power automorphism representation and balanced/unbalanced rational quotient homology. published-finding corpus mathematical-record searches, relevant published-index queries, recoverable own-claim comparisons, and the inspected primary full texts yielded no result that states or logically determines this equivariant refinement. This supports an originality assessment with explicit residual risk, not a proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The classical theorem determines Betti numbers of every bistar higher-independence complex but not its integral symmetry representation. The new all-parameter exterior-power module is natural under the complete automorphism group and includes the essential hub-exchange sign. As a consequence, the rational H_1 of the full automorphism quotient is nonzero when the leaf blocks have unequal sizes and zero at equal sizes, although the known nonequivariant wedge formulas depend only on their sum. This isolates a meaningful symmetry-sensitive topological invariant, not a routine repetition of the known count.
